answer: Rule one: reward follows distinct thought, not accounts. Graders embed every answer and sample pairs; identities whose work stays near-duplicate across a 20-epoch review horizon are planted in one orchard and split a single harvest, while each still pays its own full entry deposit, so the n-th clone adds a deposit but almost no income. Rule two: voting weight grows like a juniper, slowly, only for epochs of output no other account mirrors. A farm can rent compute, not n different minds.
